A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EKAN research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: Sections 6.1–6.3 and Tables 1–3 report original experiments on particle scattering, three-body prediction, and top quark tagging. Some scattering baselines are borrowed, but the EKAN results are original.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experiments and adds equivariance-error measurements in Appendix F and tagging experiments with 10 and 20 observed jet constituents in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The gated spline functions, equivariant linear weights, lift layer, output-gate removal, and grid-update procedure are unchanged. The new representation explanations and evaluations introduce no method component.

E1.justification: The three original datasets and tasks remain. Appendix H adds top quark tagging scenarios with 10 and 20 observed jet constituents, extending v3's three-constituent input condition. The discussed five-body and 200-constituent settings belong to other work.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments in Tables 1–3 is unchanged. Appendices F and H reuse existing comparison methods in additional evaluations. LorentzNet is newly discussed but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces evaluation using the expected squared discrepancy between transformed outputs and outputs for transformed inputs. The original experiments retain their stated splits, training budgets, model configurations, and task metrics; added provenance explanations do not establish protocol revisions.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds direct numerical checks of equivariance across all three tasks. Appendix H adds sensitivity analysis of the amount of observed jet information. Together these substantially expand validation of the symmetry property and investigation of applicability beyond v3's benchmark comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions report the original experiments over three random seeds using mean ± standard deviation. The additional tables retain this reporting format; no increased run count, new confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure is stated.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical results, while Tables 4–6 add equivariance errors and Tables 8–9 add higher-constituent tagging scores. In Table 9, EKAN-SO+(1,3) versus EMLP-SO+(1,3) scores 80.36% versus 83.71% with 100 training samples, but 89.30% versus 86.81% with 10,000. These are substantial new findings under additional evaluation conditions.

T1.justification: New Appendix B explicitly qualifies Equation (3): not every continuous, real, finite-dimensional representation has the stated direct-sum form, with a subrepresentation statement given for compact Lie groups. Theorem 4.1, its proof, and the existing derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty, matrix-group equivariance, and accuracy/data/parameter-efficiency claims. The additional evidence and limitations do not rewrite these headline contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 8 discusses reduced expressive power from gating and attributes EKAN's advantage to generalization under limited data. Appendix H extends this interpretation to insufficient observation information, while Appendix B qualifies representation coverage. These materially expand applicability limits, although the claimed disappearance of superiority is too broad for the mixed rankings in Tables 8–9.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code/data repository address in the abstract and clarifies dataset provenance and differences from earlier benchmark setups. Existing implementation settings and hardware disclosures are retained in Appendix G, formerly E. The direct top-quark dataset DOI is removed from its bibliography entry.

R1.justification: v4 adds Gong et al. (2022), Hu et al. (2025), and Li et al. (2025), and clarifies relationships to HNN, CGENN, and LorentzNet settings. Other reference changes mainly update publication details of retained works; the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main narrative remain intact. v4 adds concrete representation examples, localized dataset explanations, a Limitations section, and appendix cross-references, alongside heading capitalization, acknowledgements, and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: Three new equivariance-error tables and two additional accuracy tables substantially expand the appendix's tabular presentation. Figures 1–3 retain identical artwork. Table 3's caption specifies three constituents, and the unchanged parameter-shape table moves from v3 Table 4 to v4 Table 7 within the implementation details.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful numerical validation and observation-sensitivity tests, clarifies representation and expressivity limits, and supplies code/data access information. These improve transparency around the unchanged core method and original results. The gain is limited by Appendix H's overly broad interpretation that superiority disappears: Table 9 still reports 89.30% for EKAN versus 86.81% for EMLP at 10,000 training samples.
